messages.subject: trapping web
parts:
Background:=20
This study looks to compare deer mice density between 3 habitat treatment=
s=20
for 1 year.=20
3 treatments X 3 replications =3D 9 total 100 m2 treatment plots.

Trapping webs were placed on each treatment: 12 lines X 9 traps =3D 108=20=

traps used for 4 trap nights.

There were few captures, and I decided to pool the replications by=20
treatment.=20

Resulting data =3D 36, 42, 55 new captures for the 3 treatments respectiv=
ely.

My questions include:=20

Since I have pooled the replications,are sample sizes large enough to=20=

calculate density estimates by treatment? =09
with >60 suggested in Distance Sampling.=20=20

Also our study plots were too small as we had significant dispersal=20
between treatment trapping webs ( 20 Deer mice were caught initially in=20=

one treatment plot and recaptured in different plots. )=20
=09. Does this violate the # 2 assumption: migration through the web=20
is not allowed?=20

=09=20
=09
Within distance:=20
I have entered the data into distance and the detection functions are=20
fitting poorly.
The shape of the detection functions near zero distance (g=92(0) =3D 0),=20=

poorly fit the Shoulder=20
One treatment is above the shoulder while the other two are below.=20
I have tried various cut points and truncation with little difference in=20=

detection function.=20=20
=20=20
